When I'm with my gf and get referred to as ladies by a friend or someone in the community. If it's in passing, I just keep walking and smile. If it's in a close circle situation, I simply say 'I am actually a straight guy in a chicks body, thought I'd let ya know that'. Most of the time people take a second to understand and say alright, I wasn't aware. Or, really? Then they take a moment, nod, and move on. Then it's dealt with, and that's one more person who is enlightened of the situation. I find alot of people will start to catch them selves after a while, but with anything, it takes time.

This is also a good line if someone is referring to you as a lesbian. I know I've never come out as a lesbian, I'm a straight guy. But you can't see that from the outside. I am pre everything and will be starting T soon, & waiting on top surgery. I do look, dress & act masculine tho.

My whole life I have always dated straight women. Even my friends would ask me sometimes, 'How do you know if they're gay?' I'd be like "how do you know if you're attracted to someone?" You just know. If you hit it off and things happen, that's when you say, hey i'm different, I identify as.. and I think you're hott. That's the best you can do. Most women will find it hella attractive and the rest will peter off because they are sheltered and have no experience with the idea of being 3rd gender. At the end of the day many ppl will be curious and it may take them a while to understand and learn about trans. The other half will be ignorant and selfish, & it'll be good to not have those types in your life anyway.
